offence_severity: 3 years rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.1000/- and in default of fine to undergo additional six months imprisonment
financial_property_loss: Loss to the Depot to the tune of crores of rupees
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court did not accept the enquiry report as evidence due to the failure to prove its authenticity and the lack of proper recovery of tickets in accordance with law.
witness_credibility: PW-8 and PW-15 admitted that they were not present during the recovery of tickets and could not confirm the connection between the tickets and the accused conductors. The inspection team members also admitted that the enquiry report was only a photocopy and could not identify the accused conductors from the tickets recovered.
bail_history: They are already on bail. Their bail-bonds stand discharged.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: Not stated. Trial judgment: 28.01.2002. High Court decision: 14.09.2009. Supreme Court decision: 12.07.2022.
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Neeraj Kumar Jain, Sr. Adv., D. P. Singh, Ms. Shreya Dutt, Manu Mishra, Tavishi Kumar, Sanjay Jain, Sanjay Singh, Aniket Jain, Umang Shankar, Advs. Counsel for the State: R. K. Rathore, Ms. Jaspreet Gogia, Advs.
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Failure to prove the recovery of the tickets was validly made, failure to prove the enquiry report as only a photocopy was filed, no efforts by the prosecution to prove the existence of the original and loss thereof in order to take an order for leading secondary evidence
appeal_history: Trial court: Acquitted two Managers/Senior officials and two Inspectors, convicted rest of the eleven accused. High Court: Acquitted remaining Managers/Senior Officials, remaining two Inspectors, and three Conductors. Supreme Court: Set aside the judgment of the High Court and the trial court qua the appellants, acquitted the appellants.
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the conviction of the appellants was based on reliable, cogent, and convincing evidence led by the prosecution, including the recovery of tickets, the enquiry report, and the statements of PW-8 and PW-15. They submitted that the High Court correctly upheld the conviction based on these evidences.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the enquiry report was not properly proved as only a photocopy was filed, and the existence of the original documents and their loss were not established. They also contended that the seized tickets were not properly connected to the appellants, and the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the recovery of tickets must be validly made and that the enquiry report, if not properly proved, cannot be relied upon. The Court emphasized that the prosecution must establish the case beyond reasonable doubt.
precedent_relied_upon: Ashok Dhulichand v. Madhavrao Dube (1975) 4 SCC 664; Jai Dev v. State of Punjab AIR 1973 SC 612; Sharad Birdichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra (1984) 4 SCC 116; Sujit Biswas v. State of Assam (2013) 12 SCC 406; Samsul Haque v. State of Assam (2019) 18 SCC 161; Sarwan Singh v. State of Punjab AIR 1957 SC 637; Shivaji S. Bobade v. State of Maharashtra (1973) 2 SCC 793; Subhash Chand v. State of Rajasthan (2002) 1 SCC 702; Rajiv Singh v. State of Bihar (2015) 16 SCC 369; State of U.P. v. Wasif Haider (2019) 2 SCC 303
